title: Feeding the Gulf Coast and No Kid Hungry provide meals to kids in Vernon - NewsBreak
text: WASHINGTON COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) – The largest food bank in the Panhandle is making sure kids won’t go hungry this summer. They stopped in Vernon today to hand out free meal kits with a week’s worth of breakfasts and lunches. Feeding the Gulf Coast and No Kid Hungry partnered together to bring free meals to Vernon on Wednesday. The non-congregate meal program allows the families to take the packages home to eat at their convenience. These organizations understand that some kids will go without food when school is out. “One in five kids in our state is going hungry,” said Program Manager for No Kid Hungry, Joshua Proffitt. “So this non-congregate summer meals program is a lifeline for many families.” These organizations partnered with the Holmes Valley Church in Vernon to provide a place for community members to pick up the meals. They worked out of the church’s coffee shop called Generational Grounds. It provides a familiar place with familiar faces. “This is such a need in this area,” said volunteer Felicia Ortiz. “There are so many children that don’t have food. And with this program, we’re giving them seven days’ breakfast and lunch for seven days. So it’s a really good things for families that can’t afford it, and at least the children get food. And when they go back to school, they are all fed and healthy.” For more information about donating, volunteering, or finding help, click here .
